summary: A fully fault-tolerant implementation of the Iceberg $[[2m, 2m-2, 2]]$ quantum error-detection code applied to Toffoli and Bell state preparation circuits achieved beyond-break-even fidelity on a 36-qubit trapped-ion computer, demonstrating fidelity gains by filtering error-flagged runs. The work highlights that strategic circuit compilation for error-detection codes—particularly leveraging transversal Hadamard operations—is critical for achieving overhead-tolerant encoded circuits.
motivation: Multi-qubit gates like the Toffoli are essential for universal computation but suffer from noise accumulation on NISQ hardware. Demonstrating beyond-break-even error detection is necessary to validate the practical utility of quantum error-detection codes before advancing to full error correction.
method: Three circuit configurations were executed on trapped-ion hardware: unencoded baseline, Iceberg-encoded non-fault-tolerant, and Iceberg-encoded fault-tolerant versions of five circuits (Bell state, transversal-H Bell state, $XX$ Toffoli, $HH$ Toffoli, transversal-H Toffoli). Each configuration ran 2056 shots across three timepoints in a calibration cycle; error-flagged shots in encoded circuits were rejected before fidelity calculation.
result: Fault-tolerant Transversal-H Toffoli achieved above-break-even fidelity in all three runs ($99.17\%$, $99.75\%$, $99.61\%$ vs. $98.54\%$, $98.49\%$, $98.49\%$ unencoded baseline), with rejection rates of $80\%$–$87\%$. Transversal-H Bell state surpassed break-even in all runs; non-transversal implementations showed mixed results depending on calibration phase and circuit complexity.
